clue.text: Seen, heard, and put in one's place

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for seen is only listened to, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: seen means sighted

explanation.surface: Someone noticed, listened to, and then firmly put back in their box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in one's place' looks like a rebuke, but here it simply means located or positioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something positioned at a chosen spot is located there, as a building is placed on a plot.

clue.text: I'm safe from attack, having landed in barge

indicators.note: in puts the landed piece inside the barge

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge
acred means owning land

explanation.surface: A creature declaring itself safe now that it has come ashore in a barge.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken by the answer itself: an institution or idea immune to criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond criticism is regarded as untouchable, like the animal revered in Hinduism.

clue.text: In the end, political association is secure

parts.note: a tie is a bond or link between parties
up means over or finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A political alliance that holds firm at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something firmly with rope is to make it secure.

clue.text: Regretted doddery old peer's died

indicators.note: doddery means shaky, so the letters of old peer's are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Mourning a shaky old lord who has passed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doddery' rearranges OLDPEER to DEPLORE, and D follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to lament or strongly disapprove of it.

clue.text: Burns, say, to cut chap out

parts.note: to excise is to cut away or remove
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: An instruction to edit a man out of something, with Burns thrown in as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet Robert Burns worked as a tax officer in Scotland; 'say' marks him as one example of the type. 'Burns' tempts you towards fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns was employed collecting excise duties, so he is an example of a tax officer of that kind.

clue.text: Commonly inflames worries

indicators.note: Commonly mimics casual speech that drops the opening h

parts.note: heats means inflames

explanation.surface: Ordinary irritations stoke anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that eats at you gnaws away and troubles you, as worry does.

clue.text: A white man taking on domestic worker? No

indicators.note: taking on says the man takes the worker on in front of him

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady
a don is a gentleman, from the Spanish title
nay means no

explanation.surface: A white man asked whether he would hire a cleaner, and refusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A white' looks like part of the surface about a man; it is a white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a grape making one of the best-known white wines.

clue.text: Put energy into inadequate triangular relationship

indicators.note: Put and into together say the energy letter goes inside
into says where the energy goes: within the word for inadequate

parts.note: scant means inadequate
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Advice to work harder on a failing love triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'triangular relationship' looks like a love triangle; it is a trigonometric ratio.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the secant is a ratio of sides in a right-angled triangle.

clue.text: In struggling men, Agnes inserting a component of steel

indicators.note: inserting says the single letter goes inside the jumbled names
struggling throws the letters of men and Agnes into disorder

explanation.surface: Agnes among some struggling men, fitting a part into steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a component of steel' reads as one phrase, but its 'a' is the letter slipped into the jumbled names.
explanation.definitionFit: This metallic element is added to steel to harden and toughen it.

clue.text: Top person, or unimportant?

definitions.meaning: the person ranked first, number one, written as No. 1
a nobody, someone of no consequence

explanation.walkthrough: The number-one sense is read as No. 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Written No. 1 it is the leader; as a phrase it describes a nobody of no consequence.

clue.text: In court, no way cat's a god for Egyptian

indicators.note: In places the shortened cat within the letters for court
no tells us the abbreviation for way is to be removed from the cat

parts.note: a leopard is a big cat
RD (road) is a way
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A puzzling legal scene in which a cat is declared a god by an Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian' looks like a describing word but names the famous queen; 'no way' is a removal, not a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen famous from Shakespeare and history was a ruler of Egypt, so she is a notable Egyptian.

clue.text: Study significance of green flower

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a green traffic light signifies go

explanation.surface: A botanist studying what a green flower means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is crossword slang for a river, something that flows; the Congo is a great African river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and the Congo is one of Africa's longest rivers.

clue.text: Use me around place, only on the outside

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word me back to front
on the outside asks for only the outer letters of the word only

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrap oneself around a place, staying only on its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to use is to make use of it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Filled with depression, almost consumed by sloth

indicators.note: Filled with says the shortened word for consumed has the depression put inside it
almost removes the last letter of the word for consumed

parts.note: consumed means eaten
a dent is a depression

explanation.surface: A depressed person, nearly eaten up by idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloth' looks like laziness, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists group sloths with anteaters and armadillos as edentates, mammals lacking front teeth.

clue.text: Ranger finds a gull in lawned area

indicators.note: in places a gull inside the lawned area

parts.note: a garden is an area with lawns
a mew is a kind of gull

explanation.surface: A park ranger spots a seagull on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gull' looks like a verb meaning dupe, but it is the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranger is an officer who patrols land and protects its wildlife.

clue.text: As keyholder, very much dislike wonky nail in church

indicators.note: in places the dislike and the jumbled nail inside the church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
to hate is to dislike very much

indicators.note: wonky means crooked, so the letters of nail are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone holding the church keys who loathes a crooked nail there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As keyholder' introduces the definition: the mistress of a great house kept its keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in charge of a large house traditionally carried its keys on her belt.

clue.text: Genuine article secured by Sally say as target reserve falls short

indicators.note: secured by says the article is held inside

parts.note: an Aunt Sally is a target to throw at, so Sally's partner word is aunt
the is the definite article

indicators.note: falls short cuts the last letter off

parts.note: ice is coolness or reserve of manner

explanation.surface: A real item held by Sally, a target whose reserves are running low.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground figure people throw things at. ICE less E gives IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something authentic is real and not fake.

clue.text: Greet with small coin

parts.note: wee is Scots for small
P is a penny, a small coin

explanation.surface: Welcoming someone with a small coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' is a Scots verb meaning to cry, not to welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, to greet is to cry or shed tears, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Mine English awfully lousy, so attracting sympathy

parts.note: a pit is a mine

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of lousy are scrambled

explanation.surface: A miner speaking poor English, so drawing sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges LOUSY to OUSLY. 'so' makes the definition an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in a pitiful way, so as to arouse pity in onlookers.

clue.text: Harder to satisfy, finding nothing between chestnut and willow

indicators.note: between puts the nothing in the middle of the horse colour and the willow

parts.note: CH abbreviates chestnut, the horse colour in racing
O is zero, nothing
an osier is a willow

explanation.surface: Someone picky choosing between a chestnut tree and a willow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickier person is more selective and so less easy to please.

clue.text: Engineer's cry of amazement some may pick up

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is the engineer

indicators.note: picking up is hearing, so we want a word that sounds like the cry

parts.note: what! is a cry of amazement

explanation.surface: An engineer exclaims in surprise, and some people overhear.
explanation.walkthrough: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was a famous Scottish engineer whose name was given to the unit of power.

clue.text: Some soldiers go potty about facial hair being trimmed

indicators.note: about says the word for go potty goes around the trimmed facial hair

parts.note: to dement is to go mad, an old intransitive sense

indicators.note: being trimmed cuts the last letter off the facial hair

parts.note: a tache is a moustache

explanation.surface: Soldiers driven mad by a trimmed moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go potty' sounds like using a toilet; here it is the old verb for going mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a group of troops sent away from the main body for a task.

clue.text: Finally, he goes for plan

indicators.note: goes says the letters of he leave the phrase

parts.note: finally means in the end

explanation.surface: At last a man departs for some plan.
explanation.walkthrough: IN THE END loses HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to plan or mean to do it.

clue.text: The sign of the cross as a fertility symbol?

definitions.meaning: the lit-up walking figure at a pedestrian crossing that tells you to cross
a leafy face in old carvings, a pagan emblem of growth and rebirth

explanation.walkthrough: 'The sign of the cross' suggests a religious gesture; it is the British crossing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure lit at a pedestrian crossing and the foliate head of folklore share this name.

clue.text: Some eels are said to be cold

indicators.note: are said means we hear the word rather than see it

parts.note: jellied eels are a traditional East London dish

explanation.surface: Eels are reputed to be cold-blooded.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a London dish of eel set in jelly; JELLIED is said much like GELID.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid means icy or extremely cold.

clue.text: Get some sleep on choice blanket

indicators.note: some tells us the answer is part of the words sleep on choice

explanation.surface: Advice to snatch a nap on a fine blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like cloak with a slit for the head.

clue.text: Huge speed on old car not doing much damage

parts.note: c is the symbol for the speed of light
a heap is a battered old car

explanation.surface: A fast old banger that does little harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damage' is slang for cost, as in 'what's the damage?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexpensive does little harm to your wallet, so it costs little.

clue.text: A priest and a bishop live together

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A priest and a bishop sharing a home.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French cleric, an abbot or priest.

clue.text: Its operator turns needing coffee that's hot for a time

indicators.note: for says the hot letter replaces the time letter in the coffee

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A worker who keeps spinning round and needs a hot coffee every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' sounds like the operator spinning about, but it is woodturning.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker spins material on this machine, so its user is said to turn wood.

clue.text: People of capital settle our bill regularly in restaurants

indicators.note: settle ... in says the picked letters are lodged inside the restaurants

parts.note: diners are American roadside restaurants

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of our bill

explanation.surface: Diners paying their bill in restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle our bill' looks like paying up; it only supplies letters, picked by 'regularly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of Dublin, the Irish capital, are called by this name, as in Joyce's stories.

clue.text: Decline to add two notes to closing phrase

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
a cadence is the closing phrase of a piece of music

explanation.surface: Refusing to tack two extra notes onto a musical ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb meaning refuse; it is the noun for decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is moral or cultural decay, a falling away from former standards.

clue.text: Travel regularly again, and come back
